ReelMark Privacy Policy

Last updated: October 21, 2026

ReelMark ("ReelMark", "we", "our" or "us") is a California fishing regulations app operated by ReelRanks LLC, a California limited liability company. This policy explains what information the ReelMark app collects, how we use it, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and the choices you have. It applies to the ReelMark iOS app and the reelmark.fish website.

Information we collect

Account information. When you create an account we store your name, email address and a unique account ID. If you sign in with Apple or Google, we receive your name and email address (or Apple's private relay address) from them. We never see or store your password; Firebase Authentication handles sign-in.

Profile and preferences. Things you tell us about how you fish: experience level, angler type, favorite areas, a profile photo if you add one, your language, whether you allowed notifications and location, whether you accepted these terms, and whether you turned the AI features on.

Catch log. Each catch you log: species, length, weight, kept or released, the date, notes, a photo if you add one, and the location you confirm. If a location came from your phone's GPS or a photo's metadata, the original coordinates are stored with the catch too so you can correct the displayed location later.

Community content. Photos, captions, comments and likes you post to the community feed, plus the reports and blocks you submit. Posts and comments are shown to other signed-in ReelMark users with your first name and last initial.

Location. With your permission, ReelMark reads your phone's location while the app is open to warn you near Marine Protected Areas, show local weather, tides and ocean conditions, and pre-fill where you caught a fish. During a Fishing Mode session you start, ReelMark also reads your location in the background, on your phone only, to check Marine Protected Area boundaries and alert you; that background location is processed on the phone and is not sent to us. Your live location is not stored on our servers; only the catch locations you choose to log are.

Photos and chat text you send to the AI assistant. Photos you submit to Fish ID and the messages you send to Salty are processed by Anthropic's Claude model (see "Who we share information with"). ReelMark does not store them. A Fish ID photo is kept only if you then log the catch with it.

Feedback and support. Messages you send through Send Feedback or by email, together with your account ID.

Server logs. Our API runs on Google Cloud Run, which keeps standard request logs (timestamp, endpoint, IP address, response code) for up to 30 days for security and debugging.

What we do not collect. ReelMark has no advertising, no analytics SDK and no crash-reporting SDK, and it does not track you across other apps or websites. We do not collect your contacts or device identifiers for advertising, and background location never leaves your phone.

How we use information

  • To run the app: sign you in, show your catch log and profile, and display the community feed.
  • To show regulations, Marine Protected Area boundaries, weather, tides and ocean conditions for where you are or where you fish.
  • To identify fish from your photos and answer regulation questions through Salty.
  • To keep the community safe: review reports, enforce our Terms of Use and honor blocks.
  • To respond to your feedback and support requests.
  • We do not sell your personal information and we do not share it with advertisers.

Who we share information with

ReelMark uses the service providers below. Each receives only what it needs for its job.

  • Google Firebase (Authentication, Firestore, Storage): stores your account, profile, catch log, community content and photos. Data is stored in the United States.
  • Google Cloud Run: hosts the ReelMark API that connects the app to the services below.
  • Anthropic (Claude): receives the photos you submit to Fish ID and the text of your current Salty conversation to produce an identification or an answer. No account details are sent with them. Per Anthropic's commercial terms, data sent through the API is not used to train its models; Anthropic retains it only as described in its privacy policy at anthropic.com/privacy.
  • OpenWeather and Stormglass: receive the coordinates of the location you are viewing to return weather and ocean conditions.
  • NOAA: tide predictions come from NOAA's public service for the nearest tide station; no personal data is sent.
  • Apple and Google: handle Sign in with Apple and Sign in with Google if you choose them. On iOS, Apple's geocoding service turns catch coordinates into a place name.

We may also disclose information if required by law, to protect the rights and safety of ReelMark users, or to a successor if ReelMark is ever sold (we would tell you first).

How long we keep information

  • Your account, profile, catch log, community content and photos are kept until you delete them or delete your account.
  • You can delete individual catches, posts and comments at any time in the app.
  • Deleting your account (Settings → Delete Account) permanently removes your profile, catch log and photos, community posts, comments and likes, notifications, feedback, reports and blocks from our systems, and disconnects your Apple or Google sign-in. If others reported your content, we keep a record that a report was made and resolved, without your name or the reported text. Deletion is immediate in our database; backups and server logs age out within 30 days.
  • Photos and chat text sent to Anthropic are not stored by ReelMark. Weather and ocean lookups are cached for a few hours without any account information.

Your choices and rights

  • Edit your name and profile in the app, and change language, notification and location settings at any time.
  • Turn location, camera and photo access on or off in iOS Settings. Location is optional; the app works without it.
  • Turn the AI features (Fish ID and Salty) off in Settings → AI features. Nothing is sent to Anthropic while they are off.
  • Block users and report posts or comments from the community feed.
  • Delete catches, posts, comments or your whole account from the app.
  • Email support@reelmark.fish to ask what information we hold about you, to correct it, or to have it deleted. California residents have these rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act; we do not sell or share personal information for cross-context advertising.

Children

ReelMark is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has created an account, email support@reelmark.fish and we will delete it.

Security

Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and at rest by Google Cloud. Access to production systems is limited to ReelRanks LLC. No system is perfectly secure; if we learn of a breach affecting your information we will notify you as required by law.

Changes to this policy

We will post any changes here and update the date at the top. If a change materially affects how we use your information, we will tell you in the app before it takes effect.
